text: Jon publicly prosecutes Conor's character at length, in mock-legal register, as a recurring bit.
Heavy double-spacing after sentence-final punctuation is shared by four players (Jon 27.8, Conor 24.4, Darren 19.6, Jimmy 17.2 per 1k words); it does not identify any one of them.
Parenthetical enumeration '(1) ... (2) ...' appears in 1.1% of Jon's messages and in exactly zero messages by any other player.
Semicolon use is effectively unique to Jon (1.9 per 1k words; Conor 0.2, all others 0.0).
Jensen has the plainest vocabulary of all ten players and Jon the richest; the v1 dossiers inverted this by describing Jensen as using elevated diction.
Matt writes short messages (86 char mean, vs Jon 117) but ranks 3rd of 10 on formal connectives (0.44/1k) - brevity punctuated by occasional formal register.

Darren types chat on a phone and ballots on a desktop: 37 curly apostrophes and 6 unicode ellipses in chat with zero ASCII equivalents, against 17 straight apostrophes and 7 ASCII '...' in ballots with zero curly. No crossover.
Shane votes as often as anyone (45) but comments on only 4.4% of his ballots, the lowest rate in the league; Jon comments on 100% of his 55.
Terminal punctuation splits the group: Steiny omits it on 94.8% of messages, Jimmy 74%, Clements 71.5%, Shane on all but 4 of 522 - against Jon, who punctuates throughout.

Conor's 2026-08-27 list of 21 college-era friends is a DORKINESS ranking running #1 dorkiest to #21 coolest, not a cool ranking; Jimmy #18, Mariani #17 and Grant #19 therefore sit at the LEAST dorky end.
